description.value: The Johnson Yew and Arbutus Cabins are two adjoining modern log cabins opened in 2009 at Loon Lake Lodge & Retreat Centre, a UBC-operated wilderness retreat facility nestled in the Malcolm Knapp Research Forest roughly 50 km east of Vancouver. Together the cabins sleep up to 48 guests in shared bunkroom-style rooms, each with a writing desk and WiFi, and both buildings are connected on the ground floor with lounge areas and fireplaces. The broader Loon Lake property offers hiking, waterfront activities, sauna, and on-site dining, making it a full-service but group-oriented destination.

address.value: 14500 Silver Valley Road, Maple Ridge, BC V4R 2R3

enrichment_extras.reasoning: The website content confirms the Johnson Yew and Arbutus Cabins are real, operating accommodation at Loon Lake Lodge & Retreat Centre (UBC), with WiFi explicitly stated per-bedroom on the facilities page. No cycling-specific amenities (bike storage, tools, wash station, e-bike charging) are mentioned anywhere in the website content. The facility is a group-booking retreat and conference venue with meals-inclusive packages, not structured for individual touring cyclists passing through.
concerns: OSM lists no address or phone despite both being clearly available on the website.
OSM tags this as 'hostel' but it is a group retreat and conference centre operated by UBC — the hostel tag may be misleading.
Facility appears to operate on group-booking model; suitability for drop-in individual cyclists is unconfirmed.
enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: The cabins are a legitimate accommodation with outdoor recreation access, but the facility is structured for group retreat and conference bookings with meals-inclusive packages; it is unclear whether individual touring cyclists can book a single room without a group reservation.
